---
title: "Reading and writing data"
---

Read and write CSV and JSON, and load query results from databases.

## CSV files

`DataFrame::fromCsv()` reads delimited text the way readr's `read_csv()` and
`read_delim()` do. `DataFrame::fromCsvString()` reads from a string.
`fromCsv()` takes:

- a path, decompressing files that end in `.gz`,
- an `http://` or `https://` URL, which needs PHP's `allow_url_fopen`. The
  file is downloaded to a temporary file, read, and deleted, and a failed
  download throws with the URL and the reason,
- an open stream.

```php
$url = 'https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets'
    .'/csv/carData/Mroz.csv';
$mroz = DataFrame::fromCsv($url);
```

### Options

readr's options are named arguments in camelCase:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `types` | guess | Column types, as a compact string or by name. |
| `delimiter` | `','` | The field separator. |
| `na` | `['', 'NA']` | Text that is read as NA. |
| `colNames` | `true` | `true` reads a header row, `false` names columns `X1`, `X2`, and so on, and a list gives the names. |
| `select` | all | Columns to keep, in this order. |
| `skip` | `0` | Lines to skip before the header. |
| `nMax` | all | The most rows to read. |
| `comment` | `''` | Lines starting with this text are skipped. |
| `quote` | `'"'` | The quoting character. |
| `trimWs` | `true` | Trim spaces around unquoted values. |
| `skipEmptyRows` | `true` | Skip blank lines. |
| `guessMax` | `1000` | Rows used to guess types. |
| `nameRepair` | `'unique'` | How to repair empty or duplicated names. |
| `decimalMark`, `groupingMark` | `'.'`, none | Number formatting, as in readr's `locale()`. |

{{< include examples/_csv-options.md >}}

### Column types

`types` accepts readr's compact string, with one letter per column:

| Letter | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `c` | string |
| `i` | int |
| `d` | float |
| `n` | float, reading numbers with grouping marks and other characters |
| `l` | bool |
| `f` | factor |
| `D` | date |
| `T` | datetime |
| `t` | time |
| `?` | guess |
| `_` or `-` | skip the column |

`types` also accepts an array by column name. A value is a `Type`, a type name
such as `'factor'`, or a letter. The key `.default` sets the type of every
column not named.

{{< include examples/_col-types.md >}}

### Guessing

Without explicit types, phibble guesses each column from up to `guessMax` rows,
sampled the way readr 2 samples them. A column is:

- bool if every value is `T`, `F`, `TRUE`, `FALSE`, `True`, `False`, `true`, or
  `false`,
- int if every value is a whole number (readr guesses double),
- float if every value is a number, including `Inf` and `NaN`,
- date if every value is an ISO 8601 date,
- datetime if every value is an ISO 8601 date and time,
- time if every value is a time of day as readr reads one: hours of one or
  two digits, a colon, two digits of minutes, and optionally seconds, a
  fraction, and `AM` or `PM`, such as `7:30`, `00:07:15`, or `1:30 PM`,
- string otherwise.

Numbers with leading zeros such as `007` stay strings, as in readr.

As in readr, a time's minutes and seconds must be under 60, `12 AM` is hour
0, `PM` adds 12 hours to any hour but 12, and a fraction of a second is
dropped. The phit extension has no time type, so phibble guesses times in the
columns phit reads as text, from the same rows the PHP reader samples.

### Parse problems

When a value cannot be parsed as its column's type, a row has the wrong number
of fields, or a quoted field is never closed, phibble still returns the data.
The value becomes NA, and the read raises one `E_USER_WARNING` that lists the
problems. Rows are numbered as in `readr::problems()`: the first data row is
row 2, and skipped, blank, and comment lines are not counted.

### Quotes

Quoted fields follow readr 2's rules. A field is quoted when its first
character is the quote character. Inside a quoted field, a doubled quote is a
literal quote. Any other quote turns quoting off or back on and is dropped, so
`"x "y" z"` reads as `x y z`, and `"x "y",z"` reads as `x y,z`. A quote inside
a field that does not start with one is kept as it is. With
`escapeDouble: false`, the quotes inside a quoted field are kept, and only the
opening and closing quotes are dropped.

Files written with PHP's `fputcsv()` and its default backslash escape contain
`\"` instead of `""`. readr does not treat the backslash as an escape, and
neither does phibble unless `escapeBackslash: true` is passed.

{{< include examples/_csv-problems.md >}}

## Large CSV files

### Reading in chunks

`DataFrame::fromCsvChunked()` reads a file a chunk of rows at a time, as
readr's `read_delim_chunked()` does. It passes each chunk to a callback with
the 1-based index of the chunk's first row, and stops if the callback returns
`false`. `DataFrame::csvChunks()` returns the same chunks as a generator keyed
by that index. Memory depends on the chunk size, so a file larger than the
memory limit can be filtered down as it is read:

```php
$chunks = DataFrame::csvChunks(
    'feed.tsv',
    chunkSize: 10_000,
    delimiter: "\t",
    types: ['.default' => 'c'],
);

$kept = [];
foreach ($chunks as $chunk) {
    $kept[] = $chunk->filter(col('category')->eq('Running'));
}
$running = DataFrame::concat($kept);
```

Types not given are guessed from the first chunk, and every later chunk is
parsed as those types. As in readr, `guessMax` defaults to the chunk size.
Give every type, as above, to skip guessing. A value in a later chunk that
does not fit its column's type becomes NA. Factors without levels take their
levels from each chunk.

Every other option works as it does in `fromCsv()`. Each chunk's problems
raise their own warning, with rows numbered from the start of the file.

With the [phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit) extension loaded, chunks are read natively with `Phit\CsvReader`, with the same results
as the PHP reader.

### Memory

A whole-file read holds every value as an element of a PHP array, with either
reader, so its memory grows with the file. `fromCsvChunked()` holds one chunk
at a time, so its memory follows the chunk size. An aggregate that can be combined, such as a count or a sum, can be
computed for each chunk and the results added up. This script counts the
penguins of each species, 100 rows at a time:

{{< include examples/_chunk-totals.md >}}

For a file too large to hold as PHP arrays, keep the data in Polars, and
only the result comes back to PHP. `PolarsTable` keeps phibble's and phplyr's
API, as the [Backends](backends.qmd) page describes. phpolars'
[lazy CSV example](https://phpolars.phpstats.org/docs/examples/lazy-csv)
queries a large file with Polars' own API.

## Writing CSV

`writeCsv($path)` writes a file and `toCsv()` returns the text. The format
follows readr's `write_csv()`. Values are quoted only when needed, NA is written
as `NA`, logicals as `TRUE` and `FALSE`, dates in ISO 8601, and datetimes in
UTC with a `Z`. Times are written as hms writes a column: one number of
fraction digits for the column, and hours padded with spaces to one width.
Factors are written as their labels, and list-columns throw.

{{< include examples/_write-csv.md >}}

The options are `delimiter`, `na`, `append`, `colNames`, `quote` (`'needed'`,
`'all'`, or `'none'`), `escape`, and `eol`.

## Writing and reading JSON

`toJson()` writes a list of records, and `toJson('columns')` writes an object of
columns. NA is written as `null` and kept in every record. `DataFrame::fromJson()`
reads either shape and detects which one it has.

{{< include examples/_json.md >}}

## Databases

### Query results

`DataFrame::fromPdo()` runs a query with positional or named bindings and loads the
result. PostgreSQL and MySQL report each column's declared type, and phibble
uses it:

| Declared type | Column type |
| --- | --- |
| Text types, JSON, UUID, `TIMETZ`, intervals, arrays, and enums | string |
| `BOOLEAN` (PostgreSQL) | bool |
| Integer types and MySQL's `YEAR` | int |
| `REAL`, `DOUBLE PRECISION`, `FLOAT`, and `DOUBLE` | float |
| `NUMERIC` and `DECIMAL` | float, or int when every value is a whole number |
| `DATE` | date |
| `TIMESTAMP`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, and `DATETIME` | datetime |
| `TIME` | time |

A text column stays text, so `'TRUE'` and `'2024-01-02'` in a `TEXT` column
are strings. Only values without a declared type are guessed with the CSV
rules. SQLite stores values without a column type, so its results are always
guessed, and so are results from other drivers.

`NUMERIC` and `DECIMAL` values become doubles, as RPostgres and RMariaDB read
them:

- A value of up to 15 significant digits, such as a `NUMERIC(10,2)` price,
  reads back as the same decimal. Arithmetic on it is floating-point.
- A longer value is rounded: `12345678901234567.89` reads as
  `12345678901234568.0`.
- A `string` type keeps the database's exact decimal text.

```php
$accounts = DataFrame::fromPdo(
    $pdo,
    'SELECT id, balance FROM accounts',
    types: ['balance' => 'string'],
);
```

Explicit types always take precedence over declared ones. `fromQuery()`, the
Laravel `->toDataFrame()` macro, and `SqlTable::collect()` follow the same
rules.

{{< include examples/_pdo.md >}}

### Query builders

`DataFrame::fromQuery()` loads a query builder without depending on its library:

- A Laravel query builder, Eloquent builder, or relation is read through
  `toSql()`, `getBindings()`, and its connection's PDO object.
- A Doctrine DBAL `QueryBuilder` is read through `getSQL()` and
  `getParameters()`. Pass a PDO or DBAL connection as the second argument to
  run the SQL through PDO. Without one, the builder runs the query itself and
  phibble guesses every column, since DBAL results carry no column types.

To keep a query in the database and run verbs there, use a
[SQL table](sql.qmd) instead.

## Laravel collections

`DataFrame::fromCollection()` reads any object with an `all()` or `toArray()`
method, such as a Laravel `Collection`. The items may be arrays, objects, or
Eloquent models. `toCollection()` returns an `Illuminate\Support\Collection` of
row arrays and throws when Laravel is not installed.

{{< include examples/_collections.md >}}
